html:
Francysk Skaryna was a printer, doctor and humanist, born in Polotsk around 1490, who printed the first books of the Bible in an East Slavic language.

He studied at Kraków and took a doctorate in medicine at Padua. In Prague, from 1517, he printed more than twenty books of the Old Testament in a Church Slavonic close to the speech of his homeland, with his own prefaces and woodcuts. Around 1522 he set up the first press in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania at Vilnius, printing the Little Travel Book. His work came before any printed book in Moscow. Belarus treats him as the founder of its book culture; a state order carries his name.
sum: Francysk Skaryna was a printer, doctor and humanist, born in Polotsk around 1490, who printed the first books of the Bible in an East Slavic language.
